items.stem: What does 'double materiality' add beyond traditional financial materiality in ESG reporting?

options.text: It also considers the organisation's impacts on society and the environment, not only impacts on the company
options.rationale: Correct: double materiality covers both outward impact and financial effect on the company.

options.text: It requires reporting every topic twice
options.rationale: It is not about duplication; it is two lenses on relevance.

options.text: It removes the need for a materiality assessment
options.rationale: It shapes, not removes, the assessment.

options.text: It applies only to financial statements
options.rationale: It specifically extends beyond financial-only relevance.

items.explanation: Correct: double materiality covers both outward impact and financial effect on the company.

items.stem: Which TWO practices most improve the credibility of an ESG metric? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Documenting the metric's boundary and calculation method
options.rationale: Correct: a clear definition and boundary makes the figure comparable and checkable.

options.text: Maintaining data lineage from source system to reported value
options.rationale: Correct: traceability lets the number be verified and assured.

options.text: Rounding figures generously to look better
options.rationale: Distorting figures undermines credibility and risks greenwashing.

options.text: Reporting only the metrics that show improvement
options.rationale: Selective disclosure misleads users and damages trust.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear definition and boundary makes the figure comparable and checkable.

options.text: 'We cut Scope 1 and 2 emissions 12% versus a 2022 baseline, externally assured'
options.rationale: Correct: it is specific, scoped, baselined and evidenced by assurance.

An absolute, undefined claim cannot be substantiated.
Sentiment without evidence or metrics is not a credible disclosure.
